claims.text: Stable protective-oxide retention above 900 °C in CrFeCoNiX alloys is governed by a uniform distribution of X within a single-phase solid solution.
Al, Si, or Mn is a minor element in the proposed CrFeCoNiX alloys.
A homogeneous single-phase composition enables preferential oxidation of X.
Preferential oxidation of X produces a continuous and adherent protective oxide such as Al2O3 or SiO2.
The X-derived oxide has a thermal expansion more closely matched to the CrFeCoNiX substrate.
Improved thermal-expansion matching reduces interfacial stress.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys exhibit segregation of X or secondary phases that causes discontinuous and nonuniform oxide formation.
Variations in oxide thickness and properties create localized stresses that cause cracking or spallation.
In a homogeneous alloy, X preferentially migrates to the surface during exposure.
Formation of a dense protective external oxide can produce slow, parabolic oxidation kinetics.
Single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys will show parabolic oxide-growth kinetics and retain a continuous, adherent scale.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys will oxidize faster and may undergo breakaway oxidation, cracking, and spallation.
Previously studied multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys exhibited cracking and spallation of their surface oxides.
Exposure for approximately 50–200 hours at temperatures at or above about 900 °C is suitable for observing long-term oxidation behavior.
The exact diffusion rates of X and the relative stability of Al2O3, SiO2, and Mn oxides under the proposed conditions are uncertain.

If single-phase and multiphase samples show no significant difference in scale coherence, growth rate, adhesion, or cracking under identical conditions, the proposed control by microstructural homogeneity is falsified.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis, intervention, and boundary require temperatures above 900 °C, whereas the conditions field uses ≥900 °C and therefore includes exactly 900 °C.
